title: The UN organised Cambodia's 1993 constituent election
body: The UN Transitional Authority in Cambodia handled registration, polling and counting for elections held in May 1993. The elected assembly was charged with drawing up a constitution.
takeaway: An election for a constituent assembly chooses people to help establish the rules for future governments.
source: United Nations Archives, UN Transitional Authority in Cambodia (1992-1993)
visual: plain ballot boxes being prepared in a Cambodian schoolhall

title: In a primary cooperative, members have equal votes
body: The cooperative principles published by the United Nations give members of a primary cooperative one vote each. Members jointly own the business and take part in making its decisions.
takeaway: Equal votes give members a form of control different from voting in proportion to the money they put in.
source: United Nations, International Year of Cooperatives (2012)
visual: members sitting in a circle to discuss the running of a cooperative

title: India's Rajya Sabha is renewed in parts
body: The Rajya Sabha was first constituted in 1952. Unlike the Lok Sabha, it is a continuing body and is not dissolved for a general election. About one-third of its members retire every two years.
takeaway: Staggered terms keep some parliamentary experience in the chamber as new members arrive.
source: Parliament of India, Rajya Sabha and the Constitution of India, Article 83
visual: a curved row of desks in India's upper parliamentary chamber

title: Nine countries directly elected a shared parliament in 1979
body: In June 1979, voters in the nine European Community member states elected 410 members to the European Parliament. It was the first time those seats had been filled by direct election.
takeaway: A legislature that works across borders can give voters a direct role in choosing its members.
source: European Parliament Historical Archives, Shaping Europe
